headline: World Bank to provide $450m financing to strengthen Bangladesh’s banking sector
summary: The funding aims to protect small depositors, upgrade Bangladesh Bank's supervisory capacity, and reform state-owned banks to restore stability.
details: The World Bank has approved $450 million in financing to help Bangladesh strengthen its banking sector, which is seen as a prerequisite for reviving economic growth and job creation.

The funding, approved under Phase II of the Financial Sector Support Project, will focus on bolstering the deposit protection system to safeguard small depositors and enhancing Bangladesh Bank’s supervisory systems.
The project will also support the reform of state-owned banks and the establishment of an effective Emergency Liquidity Assistance framework to manage banking sector stress.
The World Bank noted that the sector faces significant challenges, including weak corporate governance, regulatory capture, and high non-performing loan (NPL) ratios.

As of March 2026, the NPL ratio stood at 32.6 percent, significantly higher than the South Asian average of 7.9 percent, while the system-wide capital-to-risk-weighted-assets ratio was negative 2.6 percent as of December 2025.
The project will also modernize Bangladesh Bank’s ICT infrastructure to address cybersecurity risks and close critical gaps in sector-wide data and analytics.
This initiative is part of a coordinated approach by development partners, including the IMF and the Asian Development Bank, to bolster crisis preparedness and manage financial stability.

headline_marked: Actor Zaher Alvi [[granted 2-day police remand]] over wife's suicide
headline: Actor Zaher Alvi granted 2-day police remand over wife's suicide
summary: A Dhaka court has ordered the actor to be questioned in police custody following allegations that he drove his wife, Afra Ibnat Ikra, to take her own life.
details: A Dhaka court has granted police two days of custody for actor Niamot Ullah Bhuiyan, known as Zaher Alvi, in connection with the death of his wife, Afra Ibnat Ikra.
The decision was made by Dhaka Metropolitan Magistrate Albiruni Mir on Wednesday, following a petition from the Detective Branch (DB) of the police.
Police allege that Alvi had been posting insulting and provocative content about his wife on Facebook, including a post featuring another woman on February 27.
Afra Ibnat Ikra was found dead by hanging from a ceiling fan at the family's DOHS home in Pallabi on February 28, the day after the provocative posts.
Ikra's father, Kabir Hayat Khan, filed a case alleging that his daughter was driven to suicide by prolonged family conflict and various forms of abuse.
Alvi had surrendered to the court on June 18 and his bail application was rejected, sending him to jail.
Alvi's mother, Nasrin Sultana, also surrendered on June 4 and was granted bail in the same case.
caption:
Actor Zaher Alvi is in police custody for two days after his wife's suicide. Police allege he posted insulting content on Facebook to provoke her.

A Dhaka court has granted police two days of custody for actor Niamot Ullah Bhuiyan, known as Zaher Alvi, in connection with the death of his wife, Afra Ibnat Ikra.

The decision was made by Dhaka Metropolitan Magistrate Albiruni Mir on Wednesday, following a petition from the Detective Branch (DB) of the police.

Police allege that Alvi had been posting insulting and provocative content about his wife on Facebook, including a post featuring another woman on February 27.

Afra Ibnat Ikra was found dead by hanging from a ceiling fan at the family's DOHS home in Pallabi on February 28, the day after the provocative posts.

Ikra's father, Kabir Hayat Khan, filed a case alleging that his daughter was driven to suicide by prolonged family conflict and various forms of abuse.

Alvi had surrendered to the court on June 18 and his bail application was rejected, sending him to jail.

Alvi's mother, Nasrin Sultana, also surrendered on June 4 and was granted bail in the same case.
